findings: LIBRARY DEFECT, not the paper's (strict GX/BTZ/SurfaceCompleteLip.lean, lem_surface_complete_two_lip, l.361-365): its hypothesis Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev g R) is false for EVERY g when R > 0 (GX.E0Surgery.spacelikeDevelopment_graphDev_iff : SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev g R) <-> R <= 0, no hypothesis on g). Reason: graphDev is defined on the strip (0,R] x R, which contains its rim r = R, while SpacelikeDevelopment asks the image of a neighbourhood of every point to be a full spacelike Lipschitz graph over an open set of R^2 (IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.locGraph, a surface without boundary). Proof without invariance of domain: rCoordL = t - x of the development equals r, is <= R on the image and = R at the rim point (R,0), and is constant along the developed null direction d_tau; the null line through D(g(R,0), R+eps, 0) meets the local graph near the rim point (exists_nullShift + continuousOn_nullShift) at a point of the image with rCoordL = R + eps > R (IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.exists_lt_of_null). So lem_surface_complete_two_lip is vacuously true, the row's 'Lean >= paper' claim for it does not hold, and kb lean-gx/0251's bridge cannot be proved in the form asked.

The dispatched bridge 'C^1 IsSpacelikeGraph g R => SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev g R)' is false as printed in roadmap T-btz-c1-spacelike-development (counterexample: every g, e.g. Lemma 2.6(ii)'s cusp, cusp_spacelikeDevelopment's last conjunct). Strongest true form proved: over any open Omega within {r > 0} on which g is C^1 with delta > 0, graphDevOn g Omega is a SpacelikeDevelopment (spacelikeDevelopment_graphDevOn); for a C^1 IsSpacelikeGraph g R this gives the open strip 0 < r < R (spacelikeDevelopment_openStrip), and for the cusp the whole half-plane r > 0.

Consequently 'derive the strict lem_surface_complete_two from lem_surface_complete_two_lip' is impossible (the lip lemma's hypothesis is never met), and the cusp is NOT an instance of the lip lemma. Corrected Lipschitz form proved instead: lem_surface_complete_two_unif (the strict lip proof verbatim over the two consequences of SpacelikeDevelopment it uses: UnifSpacelike g R and continuity of PulledLength.toSpace) and lem_surface_complete_two_lipOn (development spacelike over an open Omega containing the strip). It is non-vacuous: the cusp meets every hypothesis with Omega = {r > 0} (cusp_lipOn_hyps). A C^1 graph with delta > 0 on an open neighbourhood of the strip is a case (lem_surface_complete_two_of_open).

Paper, BTZ_1.tex l.781-790 (no change requested, a reading): Sigma* over D_R^* is a surface with boundary (the rim circle r = R, which completeness needs: without it a Cauchy sequence escapes through r -> R). 'Spacelike' for a non-smooth surface with boundary is therefore not Barbot's notion of an embedded spacelike Lipschitz hypersurface, which has no boundary; the readings available are 'extends across the rim' (lipOn) or 'uniformly spacelike near each point including the rim' (unif).
questions: Reading of 'spacelike' for the paper's Sigma over the closed-rim strip (l.781-786) when it is not C^1: taken here as SpacelikeDevelopment of the development over an open Omega containing (0,R] x R (Sigma extends a little across its rim as a spacelike Lipschitz surface), with the weaker UnifSpacelike + topology form also proved. The paper defines spacelike only for piecewise smooth graphs (Lemma 2.7). Which reading becomes the formalization of record, and whether the strict lem_surface_complete_two_lip should be replaced by lem_surface_complete_two_lipOn, is the author's.

kb_proposals: Causal.Flat.SpacelikeDevelopment F is a no-boundary notion: on a space with a boundary point it fails. For the btz strip, SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev g R) <-> R <= 0 for every g (GX.E0Surgery.spacelikeDevelopment_graphDev_iff); strict lem_surface_complete_two_lip is vacuous. Use SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDevOn g Omega) with an open Omega containing the strip, or UnifSpacelike g R (GXScaffold.BTZ.C1SpacelikeDevLip).

No-boundary test without invariance of domain: a continuous linear functional constant along a nonzero future causal N has no maximum on an IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn set (GX.E0Surgery.IsSpacelikeLipschitzIn.exists_lt_of_null, via exists_nullShift and continuousOn_nullShift); for the btz development use rCoordL and N = btzPaperDev (1,0,0).

The C^1 bridge: g C^1 with delta > 0 on an open Omega within {r > 0} gives SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDevOn g Omega) (GX.E0Surgery.spacelikeDevelopment_graphDevOn): zero set of nullHeightExpl g in null coordinates (no periodicity needed, fderiv_nullHeightExpl_pos), embedding read off (b, -c/max b (r0/2)).

Pulled length is monotone under inclusion of the domain: a path of the strip mapped into Omega has the same pathLength by rfl (GX.E0Surgery.edist_stripIncl_le), so continuity of PulledLength.toSpace transfers from Omega to the strip.

T-btz-cauchy-spear must not ask SpacelikeDevelopment (graphDev tau_0 R): it is unsatisfiable; ask SpacelikeDevelopment over an open Omega containing the strip (the cusp has one over r > 0) and feed lem_surface_complete_two_lipOn.

No existing file edited beyond the two import lines; no axiom; the only declaration naming a refutation is lem_surface_complete_two_lip_hyp_false / spacelikeDevelopment_graphDev_iff (it refutes a library hypothesis and the roadmap bridge, not a printed paper statement, so no not_ name). Before graduating: the strict SurfaceCompleteLip's SCOPE and the row's ledger notes describe lem_surface_complete_two_lip as 'Lean >= paper' and its hypothesis as 'expected but not proved' for C^1 graphs; both are now known false (the hypothesis is unsatisfiable). The strict lem_surface_complete_two (C^1 on the closed strip only) is still not derived from a Lipschitz form: that would need UnifSpacelike and continuity of toSpace at the rim for a C^1-within-the-closed-strip graph (a mean-value argument on the convex strip for the first; a pulled-length lower bound near the rim for the second), not attempted.
